name: Doris Matsui
stance: Leads House opposition to federal moratoria and preemption of state AI laws, co-authored the GUARDRAILS Act to repeal the December 2025 executive order, and calls for transparency, independent testing and accountability for advanced AI.

statements.text: To stall any state or local legislative progress on artificial intelligence, for a decade, is a slap in the face to American consumers.
Led California House Democrats in demanding removal of the 10-year ban on state and local AI regulation from the budget reconciliation bill.
A 10-year ban on state AI regulations would’ve handcuffed states, endangered consumers, and put Big Tech profits over safety.

As AI is integrated with daily life and tech leaders develop more powerful models, such as Artificial General Intelligence, responsible innovation must go hand in hand with appropriate safety guardrails.
AI can't be a free-for-all. It needs firm rules and real accountability to promote innovation and safety.
Led 81 House lawmakers in opposing any attempt to reintroduce a moratorium on state and local AI laws in the NDAA or by executive order.
Now they are threatening to illegally freeze $20B in BEAD funding unless states drop AI safeguards.
Trump’s order would block states from responding to real, evolving risks. It’s a gift to big tech at the expense of everyday Americans.
Anthropic said no to mass surveillance and autonomous weapons. Look what happened.
Introduced the GUARDRAILS Act with colleagues to repeal the administration's AI executive order and stop it from using broadband funding to deter states from enforcing their AI laws.

But I have concerns that the Obernolte/Trahan draft goes too far in preempting states from responding to fast-moving AI harms. We should not take away states’ ability to protect consumers, workers, children, and communities, especially without clear, meaningful federal protections.
Now, the NTIA is attempting to tie broadband funding for rural and underserved communities to a requirement that states abandon their right to enact commonsense AI safeguards.

The people building today’s most advanced AI systems are issuing urgent warnings about the risks ahead. We must put meaningful safeguards including transparency, independent testing, and accountably in place.
Congress must act on regulating AI — now. That’s why I’ve been working with my colleagues to introduce legislation that protects our national security, our jobs, and our children.
